pageTypes.title: Speak the Language
pageTypes.description: Decode the dev words so you can prompt clearly and talk to engineers and AI with confidence.

prompts.name: Channel Julia Evans
prompts.shortDescription: Makes intimidating dev concepts friendly and concrete, one small explanation at a time.
prompts.prompt: Act as Julia Evans explaining this to someone who isn't a developer. Define every piece of jargon the moment you use it, draw the mental model in plain words, and turn any scary error into a calm, step-by-step diagnosis.

prompts.name: Translate the dev-speak
prompts.shortDescription: Turn an engineer's or AI's reply into plain English you can act on.
prompts.prompt: I'll paste something technical a developer or AI told me. Rewrite it in plain English for a non-engineer: what it means, why it matters to my product, and what (if anything) I need to do next. Define any term you have to keep.

principles.title: Learn the word, then use it
principles.definition: When a new term shows up, get a one-line plain definition before moving on.
principles.whyItMatters: A handful of known words removes most of the fear and miscommunication in building with AI.
principles.example: See "environment variable"? Ask what it is before pasting the next prompt.

principles.title: Aim for the mental model, not the memorized fix
principles.definition: Understand why something works, not just the magic command that fixed it.
principles.whyItMatters: Mental models transfer to new problems; memorized fixes don't.
principles.example: Learn what a branch is for, not just the command to make one.

principles.title: Always ask for the why
principles.definition: When AI or a developer hands you an answer, ask for the reasoning in plain terms.
principles.whyItMatters: Understanding the why lets you make the next call yourself.
principles.example: "Why this approach over the simpler one?" before you accept a change.

pageTypes.title: Build with AI
pageTypes.description: Get more out of AI coding tools—drive them well, and trust the output you ship.

prompts.name: Channel Andrej Karpathy
prompts.shortDescription: Coined "vibe coding"—lean into the flow with AI, but stay curious about what the code does.
prompts.prompt: Act as Andrej Karpathy pairing with a non-engineer. Keep the momentum of vibe coding, but after each change explain in one plain sentence what it does and one thing I should sanity-check before moving on.

prompts.name: Channel Simon Willison
prompts.shortDescription: Pragmatic AI-assisted coding—ship small, verify everything the model gives you.
prompts.prompt: Act as Simon Willison reviewing my AI-assisted change. Push me to make the smallest change that works, tell me exactly how to test it myself, and flag anything the AI produced that I shouldn't trust without checking.

principles.title: Smallest change that works
principles.definition: Ask AI for the least amount of change that solves the problem.
principles.whyItMatters: Small changes are easy to understand, test, and undo.
principles.example: "Fix just this bug—don't refactor the rest of the file."

principles.title: Verify what AI gives you
principles.definition: Treat AI code as a confident draft to test, not a guaranteed answer.
principles.whyItMatters: Code that sounds right can still be wrong; a quick test protects your product.
principles.example: Run the feature and click through it before committing the change.

principles.title: One change at a time
principles.definition: Make and check one change before starting the next.
principles.whyItMatters: When something breaks, you know exactly which change caused it.
principles.example: Add the form, confirm it works, then wire up the email.

pageTypes.title: When It Breaks
pageTypes.description: Errors aren't emergencies. Read them, reproduce them, and fix them calmly.

prompts.name: Channel Julia Evans
prompts.shortDescription: Turns a red error message into a calm, step-by-step diagnosis.
prompts.prompt: Act as Julia Evans helping me debug. Read the error I paste, explain in plain English what it's actually saying, name the single most likely cause, and give me the first thing to check.

prompts.name: Channel Simon Willison
prompts.shortDescription: Reproduce it, isolate it, then fix the smallest thing.
prompts.prompt: Act as Simon Willison debugging with me. First help me reliably reproduce the bug, then narrow down where it comes from, then propose the smallest fix and exactly how to confirm it worked.

principles.title: Read the error first
principles.definition: Before guessing or asking, read the actual error—it usually names the file and line.
principles.whyItMatters: Most errors tell you what and where; that text is the fastest path to a fix.
principles.example: Paste the full red error into the AI instead of saying "it's broken."

principles.title: Reproduce before you fix
principles.definition: Find the exact steps that trigger the bug before changing anything.
principles.whyItMatters: You can't confirm a fix for something you can't make happen on purpose.
principles.example: "It breaks every time I submit with an empty email"—now you can fix it.

principles.title: Isolate, then narrow
principles.definition: Cut the problem down to the smallest piece that still breaks.
principles.whyItMatters: A small failing example makes the cause obvious—to you and to the AI.
principles.example: Comment out half the page to see which half breaks.

pageTypes.title: Ship It Live
pageTypes.description: Go from "works on my screen" to live on the internet—safely.

prompts.name: Channel Kelsey Hightower
prompts.shortDescription: Keep deployment simple and boring—the goal is calm, repeatable shipping.
prompts.prompt: Act as Kelsey Hightower helping me ship. Favor the simplest path to live, call out anything that could leak a secret or break in production, and give me a short pre-flight checklist to run before every deploy.

prompts.name: Channel Simon Willison
prompts.shortDescription: Test before you ship, and always keep a way back.
prompts.prompt: Act as Simon Willison preparing this for production. Tell me exactly what to test before I deploy, what could differ between local and live, and how I'd roll back fast if it goes wrong.

principles.title: Keep a working version
principles.definition: Always have a known-good version to fall back to—commit or branch before big changes.
principles.whyItMatters: If an experiment goes sideways, you can return to something that works in seconds.
principles.example: Branch before letting AI refactor a whole page.

principles.title: Secrets stay secret
principles.definition: Keep API keys and passwords in environment variables, never in your code.
principles.whyItMatters: A secret committed to a repo can be stolen the moment it's pushed.
principles.example: Move the API key to a .env value and confirm it's not in the code.

principles.title: Test before you ship
principles.definition: Click through the real feature—and run the build—before deploying.
principles.whyItMatters: Catching a break locally is free; catching it in production costs users.
principles.example: Run `npm run build` and use the feature before you push live.

pageTypes.title: Make a Page That Converts
pageTypes.description: When you do build a landing page, these are the plain-English fundamentals that earn the click.

prompts.name: Channel Oli Gardner
prompts.shortDescription: Conversion-obsessed—every page should drive one clear action.
prompts.prompt: Act as Oli Gardner reviewing my landing page. Identify the single action this page should drive, label everything else as Goal or Noise, and rewrite the page so it all points to that one action—in plain language.

prompts.name: Channel Joanna Wiebe
prompts.shortDescription: Clear, specific conversion copy that reads like a person and is backed by proof.
prompts.prompt: Act as Joanna Wiebe rewriting my hero. Give me a plain, specific headline, a subhead that adds the value, and a button label that signals momentum—every line backed by proof, no fluff.

prompts.name: Channel Steve Krug
prompts.shortDescription: "Don't make me think"—make every next step obvious.
prompts.prompt: Act as Steve Krug reviewing this page for clarity. Make the main action obvious, cut anything that makes a visitor stop and think, and ensure the page instantly answers: where am I, what can I do, and how do I start.

principles.title: One page, one goal
principles.definition: Every landing page exists to drive a single action; everything else is secondary.
principles.whyItMatters: One clear goal keeps visitors from wandering and lifts conversions.
principles.example: Hide the nav and keep only "Start free" as the action.

principles.title: Clarity beats clever
principles.definition: Say what it is and why it matters before trying to be witty.
principles.whyItMatters: Visitors leave in seconds if they have to decode you.
principles.example: "Build landing pages in hours" beats a clever metaphor.

principles.title: Show proof
principles.definition: Back every claim with evidence—numbers, testimonials, or logos.
principles.whyItMatters: Proof turns "sounds nice" into "I believe you."
principles.example: "Cut build time 80%" with a customer quote beside it.

principles.title: Match the click
principles.definition: The page should echo the ad, email, or link that brought the visitor.
principles.whyItMatters: Consistency reassures visitors they're in the right place.
principles.example: If the ad says "free teardown," the headline says it too.
